findings.issue: ALLOWED_DIRS names the whole of plugins/audit/evals/, and _coverable_test_names() walks every file under it. That includes the gitignored evals/results/ directory that `claude plugin eval` writes on one machine (.gitignore:65). Any file name written there becomes a name a tests/test_*.py is allowed to carry. A stray orphan test file could therefore pass the orphan check on a machine that has run the eval and fail it on CI, which has not. Nothing real is hidden today, because the new coverage cases read only the tree as committed. It is the same machine-dependence class the classifier otherwise avoids by reading the checkout.
findings.resolution: Make the evals walk skip `results` (prune it from `dirnames` for that directory), or derive the allowed names from tracked files only. Add one case to tests/test__output_lints.py: a file under `<evals>/results/` must not make a same-named suite a non-orphan.

intent.redFirstBasis: The executor's filed redFirst is `could-not-prove`. At HEAD the suite's output carried two runners' tallies (house 'SELFTEST FAILED: 1/25' and unittest 'Ran 0 tests'), and the command names neither, so whose failing cases were whose could not be told. That basis holds as stated. The test file was changed after filing (quoted() folds every child output onto its case's own line; esc24 holds that through _runner_output.read_tally). So the proof on record is could-not-prove and will be taken again on the final file. What I established myself: I ran `python3 tests/test_build_shop.py --selftest` once on the tree as it stands. It printed ALL PASS: 28/28, and esc24 passed, reading the raw fixture transcript as 'unittest' and the folded FAIL line as 'house'. That is a green run only. I did not see any added test red, and I did not re-derive the executor's 26-row mutation table, so I report no proved red. By reading: each refusal case (esc20, esc21, esc22) patches a COPY of the builder and asserts its anchor matched exactly once (hits == 1) before reading the exit code, so a patch that never landed fails the case instead of passing it. Each refusal also has an allow twin (esc17, esc1, esc8). The classifier cases' ability to fail rests on the same executor table, so I record nothing beyond reading it.

In tests/test__output_lints.py I read only the selftest_coverage region: _sc_tree and cases sc1 to sc13 (lines ~990-1100) read against the classifier code. Those pre-existing cases would fail if the evals walk or the real-default logic were removed (sc7 and sc13 on the real tree; sc10 and sc12 on fixtures). I did not read the rest of that file's cases, which are lint cases about other behaviours the gate command does not name as this task's behaviour, so for them the answer is an unread scope, not a read result. That is over-firing, not a test that cannot fail.
